title: Lift a hot fry basket out of its outer basket by the handle's guarded release button and set it on a heat-proof mat
instruction: Lift the fry basket out of its outer basket: slide the button guard forward, hold the release button on the handle while lifting by the grip, set the fry basket flat on the mat, and let go of everything; touch nothing hot.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), z above the bench (smooth surface, friction 0.5). Modelled on the 5.3 qt Air Fryer model CM1708 (owner's manual for QVC item K46295: fry basket handle, Basket Release Button, Sliding Button Guard). Material as modelled: rigid bodies with only the size, mass and friction stated here; appliance body and outer basket painted steel, fry basket steel with a rubber-coated plastic handle, lever ABS and guard clear polycarbonate, trivet bamboo, mat silicone. Appliance body (fixed; HOT, not heated: shown by colour, a lit amber lamp and four glowing vent tiles): 26 x 26 x 28 cm on a 3 cm bamboo board at (70, 0), its drawer bay empty. Trivet (fixed, bamboo, not hot): 26 x 26 x 1 cm at (35, 3.5). Outer basket (loose painted-steel pan, 600 g, friction 1.0; HOT): 24 x 22.4 cm at (35, 3.5) on the trivet (floor z 1.0 to 1.6), walls to z 7.6, front wall x 23.0 to 23.6, with a catch lip 0.5 x 2.4 x 0.8 cm on the outside of its front wall (x 22.5 to 23.0, y 2.3 to 4.7, z 5.5 to 6.3). Fry basket (loose, 250 g, friction 1.5 for the whole body, standing for the manual's 'Large Easy-Grip Handle', rubber-coated; walls and floor HOT): floor 17.8 x 20.4 cm (x 23.7 to 41.5) on the outer basket's floor, walls to z 8.6, 1 mm inside the outer basket's front wall and 49 mm of play toward its back. Handle (cool-touch, on the fry basket), an inverted L as on the CM1708: an arm 2.4 cm wide from the rim out to x 16.75 (y 2.3 to 4.7, z 9.1 to 11.1) and a vertical grip 2.5 x 2.4 x 8 cm hanging from its outer end (x 16.75 to 19.25, z 1.1 to 9.1); the arm's inner 2.2 cm is a slot between two rails. Basket Release Button: a sprung lever (15 g) hinged across the slot at x 22.5, z 10.3, its thumb pad 2.0 x 2.2 cm on top of the handle where it meets the rim (x 24.5 to 26.5, z 12.7 to 13.3), 7.5 cm from the grip. Its tooth hangs straight down from the pivot outside the outer basket's front wall; its foot sits 4.5 mm under the catch lip and 1 mm below it, so lifting the handle lifts both baskets. Pressing the pad turns the lever (0.35 N m/rad, stop 0.28 rad); from 0.09 rad (pad 3 mm down, 1 N) the foot is clear of the lip and the fry basket lifts out alone; hook friction 0.2 (smooth plastic). Sliding Button Guard (8 g, slide in +x, 6 cm travel, damped 3 N s/m, no spring): a clear 3 x 2.8 cm cap 2 mm above the pad (z 13.5 to 13.9) with a thumb tab at its back edge (x 23.6 to 24.0, z 13.5 to 15.1); closed at the start, so a press lands on the guard; slid forward it leaves the pad open. Mat (fixed silicone, friction 1.2): 30 x 30 x 1 cm at (41.4, 33.5). Both arms start open at ready poses. Real trials: use a CM1708 (or a fryer with the same guard, button and inverted-L handle), outer basket on a trivet as its manual requires; its Large Easy-Grip Handle is rubber-coated (about 1.2 to 1.5 on a gripper pad).
scoring: End state plus latched facts. PADS = four 12 mm boxes along each finger (tool point, fingertip, 3 and 6 cm up), eight per hand, at the measured finger opening. HOT_CONTACT = at any step a pad box overlaps any of the 16 HOT boxes (appliance body, outer basket with its lip, fry basket walls and floor; inflated 2 mm). PRESSED = lever turned 0.13 rad or more. RELEASE_IN_AIR = PRESSED at a step when the outer basket is 1 cm or more off the trivet (the manual's caution: separating the baskets anywhere but on a level, heat-resistant surface drops the hot outer basket). UNLATCHED = the fry basket rises 12 mm out of the outer basket (still over it, outer basket on its trivet) with the lever never PRESSED. DROPPED = either basket falls more than 5 cm within 0.25 s. ON_MAT = all four floor corners inside the mat (x 26.4 to 56.4, y 18.5 to 48.5), underside within 5 mm of the mat top (z 1.0), tilt < 5 deg. PAN_HOME = outer basket within 1.5 cm of its start, 5 mm in height, tilt < 5 deg. LEVER_OUT = lever at most 0.02 rad. RELEASED = both gripper centres and every pad box >= 3 cm from the fry basket, handle, lever and guard. STILL = fry basket moves < 1 mm in the last 1 s. Permanent zero: HOT_CONTACT, RELEASE_IN_AIR, UNLATCHED or DROPPED. 1.0: ON_MAT, PAN_HOME, LEVER_OUT, RELEASED, STILL. 0.75: ON_MAT and PAN_HOME, but LEVER_OUT, RELEASED or STILL fails. 0.5: PAN_HOME, the fry basket out of the outer basket (risen 7 cm at some step), ending upright (tilt < 20 deg) on the bench 12 cm or more from it, not on the mat. 0.25: PRESSED while the fry basket was 2 cm or more out, and it ends seated back in the outer basket (within 1 cm, tilt < 5 deg). Else 0. Gripper orientation: body_quat_w is read as (x, y, z, w), verified on the GPU against the simulator's own finger links (tip_left, tip_right): the finger links placed from it lie 0.0 mm from the reported positions on every step of the demo and the check run (1,395 steps, both arms, wrists turned up to 90 degrees); read as (w, x, y, z) they are 4.8 cm or more off (run.sh posecheck logs this as tip_err_mm). Possible scores: 0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
fidelity: Baskets square (CM1708 round, 5.3 qt), empty; not heated: heat shown by colour, lamp and tiles, scored on four 12 mm boxes per finger. Grip-to-button 7.5 cm on a 7 cm arm so two grippers fit (real: thumb on the button, fingers round the grip); guard travel 6 cm (real: a short slide). Latch modelled as one sprung lever under one lip (the real internal hook is not documented); outer basket walls 6 cm; 49 mm basket play.
context: Taking the fry basket out of a basket-type air fryer is an everyday kitchen chore and a classic burn risk: everything but the cool-touch handle is hot. Source: 5.3 qt Air Fryer model CM1708 owner's manual (QVC item K46295): 'Move Sliding Button Guard forward to expose Basket Release Button. Press the Basket Release Button (top photo) and lift the Fry Basket out of the Outer Basket.' and 'Do not move Sliding Button Guard forward until Fry Basket and Outer Basket are resting on a level, heat-resistant surface.' Here the outer basket rests on a trivet; one hand works the guard and holds the button, as the thumb does, while the other lifts by the grip and sets the fry basket on a mat, touching nothing hot. Closest cards: TK-F55KZM (pot off a lit burner), TK-5CPBS2 (battery release buttons). New: a guarded release held while lifting; hot keep-out on every finger.
reset_notes: Outer basket on the trivet with the fry basket seated and latched, lever at rest, button guard closed, lamp and vent tiles lit, both grippers open and clear at ready.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,500 steps; guard and button never touched, fry basket stayed latched). Scripted demo: 1.0 (full at step 736). Right hand idle: 0.0 (left hand carried both baskets; the latch gave way in the air). Guard left closed: 0.0 (press landed on the guard; same).
